quests.instruction: Touch the school word for the person who drives the school bus safely!
quests.question: Bus Driver
quests.hint: This person sits at the front of the bus, holding the big wheel.
quests.explanation: That's right! A bus driver makes sure every student gets home safely.
quests.funFact: A bus driver often learns the names of every student who rides their bus!

quests.instruction: Touch the school word for the subject where we practice books and stories!
quests.question: Reading
quests.hint: This subject is all about books, letters, and stories.
quests.explanation: That's right! We sound out words and enjoy stories during reading class.
quests.funFact: The more you practice reading, the faster you can recognize new words!

quests.instruction: Point to the seat every student has next to their desk!
quests.question: Chair
quests.hint: Every desk in the classroom has one sitting right next to it.
quests.explanation: Correct! A chair and a desk almost always sit right next to each other.
quests.funFact: Some classroom chairs are stacked together and stored when they're not needed!

quests.instruction: Touch the little bag that keeps our pencils and erasers together!
quests.question: Pencil Case
quests.hint: It usually has a zipper to keep everything safely inside.
quests.explanation: Yes! A pencil case keeps our pencils, erasers, and rulers together in one spot.
quests.funFact: Some pencil cases can stand up on their own like a little box!

quests.instruction: Find the word for the place where we borrow books to read!
quests.question: Library
quests.hint: You must stay quiet here so everyone can read in peace.
quests.explanation: Well done! A library keeps rows and rows of books for everyone to enjoy.
quests.funFact: A library can hold thousands of books for students to borrow and enjoy!

quests.instruction: Find the tool you hold to draw a picture of your family!
quests.question: Pencil
quests.hint: You hold it between your fingers and press it gently on paper.
quests.explanation: Yes! A pencil is the tool we use to write words and draw pictures.
quests.funFact: The soft grey part inside a pencil is called graphite, not lead at all!

quests.instruction: Point to the tool that helps our art projects stay stuck in place!
quests.question: Glue Stick
quests.hint: It helps two pieces of paper stay joined together, like magic!
quests.explanation: Correct! A glue stick is perfect for sticking paper without any mess.
quests.funFact: A glue stick dries clear, so you can barely see it on your paper!

quests.instruction: Touch the school word for the long path that connects every classroom!
quests.question: Hallway
quests.hint: This long space connects one classroom to the next classroom.
quests.explanation: That's right! We walk through the hallway to get to our next class.
quests.funFact: Some school hallways are decorated with colorful student artwork on the walls!

quests.instruction: Find the tool that draws thick, colorful lines on paper or a board!
quests.question: Marker
quests.hint: It has a cap you must remember to put back on.
quests.explanation: Yes! A marker draws bold, colorful lines on paper or a whiteboard.
quests.funFact: Some markers even smell like fruit, such as strawberry or grape!

quests.instruction: Touch the word for the vehicle with rows of seats that drives us home!
quests.question: School Bus
quests.hint: It is big, often yellow, and has many seats inside.
quests.explanation: Yes! A school bus is the big vehicle that carries students to and from school.
quests.funFact: School buses are often painted bright yellow so drivers can spot them easily!

quests.instruction: Touch the word for the place where lunch trays are carried to a table!
quests.question: Cafeteria
quests.hint: This big room has many tables where students sit to eat.
quests.explanation: Yes! A cafeteria is the room where students sit down to eat lunch.
quests.funFact: Some school cafeterias can serve lunch to hundreds of hungry students every day!

quests.instruction: Touch the school word for the subject where we practice making letters and sentences!
quests.question: Writing
quests.hint: This subject is all about letters, sentences, and your very own stories.
quests.explanation: That's right! We use a pencil to practice writing during this subject.
quests.funFact: Learning to write neatly takes practice, just like learning to read does!

quests.instruction: Point to the word for the peaceful moment when a picture book comes to life!
quests.question: Story Time
quests.hint: Your teacher often reads a picture book aloud during this time.
quests.explanation: Yes! Story time is when our teacher reads us a favorite tale aloud.
quests.funFact: Listening to stories can introduce you to brand new words you've never heard before!

quests.instruction: Point to the word for the subject where every letter must sit in just the right spot!
quests.question: Spelling
quests.hint: You practice new words each week during this subject.
quests.explanation: Yes! Spelling is the subject where we practice putting letters in the right order.
quests.funFact: Practicing a new word a few times can help you remember how to spell it!

quests.instruction: Touch the school word for the room where we paint and make crafts!
quests.question: Art Room
quests.hint: This room is often colorful, with paint, brushes, and paper everywhere.
quests.explanation: That's right! We create paintings and crafts inside the art room.
quests.funFact: Art rooms often have sinks nearby so students can wash paint off their hands!

quests.instruction: Find the word for the person who checks a small cut or a tummy ache!
quests.question: School Nurse
quests.hint: This person often has bandages ready to help with a small scrape.
quests.explanation: Well done! A school nurse helps keep every student healthy and safe.
quests.funFact: A school nurse often keeps a cozy cot ready for students who need a short rest!

quests.instruction: Touch the small stick that writes in white or color on a board!
quests.question: Chalk
quests.hint: A wet or dry cloth can wipe its marks away easily.
quests.explanation: Well done! Chalk helps a teacher write a lesson for the whole class to see.
quests.funFact: Chalk is made from a soft rock that can be ground into a stick!

quests.instruction: Touch the flat holder that keeps our loose papers from getting lost!
quests.question: Folder
quests.hint: It keeps your worksheets flat and safe inside your backpack.
quests.explanation: Well done! A folder protects our papers on the way to and from school.
quests.funFact: Some folders have pockets on both sides to sort different papers!

quests.instruction: Touch the word for the fun outdoor spot we visit during recess!
quests.question: Playground
quests.hint: This is an outdoor spot with slides, swings, and lots of running.
quests.explanation: Yes! A playground is the outdoor place where we play during recess.
quests.funFact: Many playgrounds have slides, swings, and climbing bars all in one place!

quests.instruction: Point to the word for the subject where a simple question can lead to a big discovery!
quests.question: Science
quests.hint: You might learn about plants, animals, or weather during this class.
quests.explanation: Yes! Science is the subject where we explore plants, animals, and how things work.
quests.funFact: Scientists ask questions and test ideas, just like students do in science class!

quests.instruction: Touch the tool with soft bristles that spreads paint onto our paper!
quests.question: Paintbrush
quests.hint: After painting, it needs a good rinse in water to get clean.
quests.explanation: Well done! A paintbrush's soft bristles help spread color evenly.
quests.funFact: Paintbrush bristles can be made from soft animal hair or from nylon!

quests.instruction: Point to the flat surface where a student sits down to work!
quests.question: Desk
quests.hint: You place your notebook and pencil on it before you start writing.
quests.explanation: Correct! A desk is where a student's books and pencils usually sit.
quests.funFact: The word desk comes from an old word meaning a table for writing!

quests.instruction: Point to the tool with a handle for each of your fingers!
quests.question: Scissors
quests.hint: It is always used slowly and carefully, with an adult nearby to help.
quests.explanation: Correct! Scissors are always used slowly and carefully in the classroom.
quests.funFact: School scissors often have rounded tips to help keep little fingers safe!

quests.instruction: Point to the word for the little pause when tummies get a small, tasty treat!
quests.question: Snack Time
quests.hint: You might eat crackers, fruit, or a small treat during this time.
quests.explanation: Yes! Snack time is the short break when we enjoy a small, healthy bite.
quests.funFact: Fruits like apples and grapes make popular, healthy choices for snack time!

quests.instruction: Touch the word for the person who keeps every book on its shelf!
quests.question: Librarian
quests.hint: This person knows exactly where every book belongs on its shelf.
quests.explanation: Yes! A librarian takes care of the library and helps us find books.
quests.funFact: A librarian often knows hundreds of book titles and where each one belongs!

quests.instruction: Point to the board that becomes clean again with just one wipe!
quests.question: Whiteboard
quests.hint: Markers write on it easily, and a wipe cleans it right off.
quests.explanation: That's right! A whiteboard lets a teacher write and then wipe it clean.
quests.funFact: Some whiteboards are magnetic, so little magnets can stick to them too!

quests.instruction: Point to the word for the moment chairs are pushed aside for a friendly circle!
quests.question: Circle Time
quests.hint: This often happens in the morning before lessons begin.
quests.explanation: Yes! Circle time is when the whole class sits together in a circle to share.
quests.funFact: Sitting in a circle lets every student see each other's friendly faces!

quests.instruction: Touch the thin sheet a pencil or crayon can leave a mark on!
quests.question: Paper
quests.hint: A pencil, crayon, or marker leaves its mark right on this.
quests.explanation: That's right! We use paper for writing letters and drawing pictures.
quests.funFact: Paper was first made from tree bark, plants, and old cloth long ago!

quests.instruction: Point to the bag we pack with pencils, books, and snacks each morning!
quests.question: Backpack
quests.hint: You pack it in the morning and open it again after school.
quests.explanation: Correct! A backpack keeps our school things together in one safe place.
quests.funFact: Some backpacks have a special pocket just the right size for a water bottle!

quests.instruction: Touch the colorful liquid we spread on paper with a brush!
quests.question: Paint
quests.hint: It comes in small pots or tubes of every color.
quests.explanation: Well done! Paint fills a picture with bright, wet color.
quests.funFact: Paint dries as the water inside it slowly disappears into the air!
